Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 91, verse 1–10:

Name of the Surah

• It is called "al-Shams" (the Sun), because it opens with Allah's oath by the sun, shining brightly at the time of the forenoon (duha).

From the Objectives of the Surah

• To point to the conditions of people and their ranks along the paths of guidance and misguidance, and happiness and wretchedness, and to affirm this by swearing by exalted things, which demonstrate the wondrous creation of Allah the Exalted and His uniqueness in divinity.

[The Tafsir]

Allah swears by the sun and its daylight and its brightness in the forenoon, and by the moon when it follows it in its rising and its setting, and by the day when it reveals and uncovers the darkness, and by the night when it covers the earth so that what is upon it becomes dark, and by the sky and its firm construction, and by the earth and its spreading out, and by every soul and Allah's perfecting of its creation to perform its duty, so He made clear to it the path of evil and the path of good. Whoever purifies it and causes it to grow in goodness has succeeded, and whoever buries it in sins has failed.

Thamud denied their prophet, having reached the utmost in disobedience, when the most wicked of the tribe rose up to hamstring the she-camel. The messenger of Allah, Salih (peace be upon him), said to them: "Beware of touching the she-camel with harm, for she is a sign (ayah) that Allah has sent to you, testifying to the truthfulness of your prophet. And beware of transgressing against her water, for she has a day's share of water and you have a known day's share." It grieved them, so they denied him regarding what he had threatened them with, and they slaughtered her. So their Lord overwhelmed them with punishment for their crime, levelling it upon them equally, and not one of them escaped. And He—exalted is His power—does not fear the consequence of what He sent down upon them of severe punishment.
